## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_劫财 (Metal carrying The Rival). Persona The Rival (劫财). Definition line: "Same nature, different register, the edge of comparison". Keyword Rivalry, charge fierce, poles catalyst Daring / friction Drain. Family function: Body. Cost dimension: comparison as fuel; the race never announces a finish. Arena: the race, the shared prize, the other runner. Classical portrait: same nature, different register; comparison as fuel; the race with no announced finish. Ruled domains: Rivalry, Shared stakes, Boldness. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 比肩.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Metal meeting Metal cross-polarity — similar nature, competitive register".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the Rival: an edge that sharpens against other edges. Competition wakes you up, stakes clarify you, and you cut boldest when something real is on the table. Money and metal both change hands fast around you. The trick of your life is dueling without wounding, and betting without handing over the sword."
- k2_functional: "Your energy spikes for contests and crashes after. Build recovery into the schedule like a trainer would."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Keeps score","Bets the rent","Hates to lose"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Rivalry":"Rivalry is your whetstone: you improve fastest with a named competitor in view. Choose rivals worth becoming, because you will absorb their shape. And retire each rivalry the day it stops sharpening and starts nicking.","Shared stakes":"You bet alongside people easily: ventures, splits, loans between friends. Metal keeps clean edges, so keep clean papers. The partnerships that survive you are the ones with terms as sharp as the trust.","Boldness":"Your nerve is surgical: boldest when the cut is clear. Practice sizing the wager to the blade. Full force is for openings that deserve it, not for every glinting chance."}

Making a thing yourself feels safer than being measured on it, so you build alone rather than with help. Let one favour into the making, because you pay most for the things you make alone."

Core element Metal, energy element Metal. Law: Metal and Metal are the same element (the self pair). Relative to the core the energy is the self, so Metal is this core's Body. value.text: You compete best with someone to beat and know it. Knowing where you stand matters more than comfort, so you compete harder against one rival than for any reward. Pick one contest with a finish line, because yours have no end in sight.

value_b.text: Competing against someone moves you faster than any praise. Since you carry little Metal, you would rather borrow strength from a contest than from comfort. Compete with someone who also wants you to win, because you run a race that never announces a finish.

value.text: For you, competing with a friend is taking them seriously. You raise the stakes out of wanting someone worth beating more than someone easy to keep. Keep one friend outside the contest, as you cost a rival the ease of siding with you.

value.text: Your yes to a bet comes before the fear has finished. Hesitating feels like losing to yourself, so you bet first and size it afterwards. Keep one bet a year you can afford to lose, since nerve costs you money as much as pride.

value_b.text: Being first to bet is the part you enjoy. Betting first gives you strength where waiting gives none, and the bold move comes ahead of the sure one. Let one sure thing count, because you never count wins you did not bet on.

value.text: You trust a person faster when the risk is shared. Sharing the risk makes the bond real to you, so you go in together ahead of writing anything down. Write the terms down once, because you risk the friendship as much as the money.

value_b.text: A shared risk is your fastest way into partnership. Being in it together matters more than being safe, and you split the stakes before the roles. Keep the roles clear, because you lose friends in a loose deal as easily as cash.

value.text: Where a friend needs backing, you share the risk first. Sharing the risk feels closer than staying out, and the shared bet comes before your margin. Keep one account no friend can draw on, since you cover their losses with money meant for rest.

value.text: Sharing a risk with someone is your warmest offer. Wanting them in it more than safe from it, you share the upside and the fall. Say the downside first, as you bring the people you like into risks sized to your nerve.
